key_insight: A symmetry-aware single-orbital tight-binding model can reproduce the low-energy band structure and spin splitting of chiral one-dimensional hybrid lead halide perovskites using only a few effective hopping terms.
engineering_relevance: This gives a compact, physically transparent model for predicting and tuning band-edge electronic, spin, and transport behavior in chiral perovskite optoelectronic devices.
method: Built a single-orbital tight-binding Hamiltonian on four symmetry-related sites per primitive cell.
Included layer, in-plane sublattice, and spin degrees of freedom with separate parameter sets for conduction and valence bands.
Analyzed degeneracies using screw eigenvalues and antiunitary symmetry operators to distinguish accidental from symmetry-enforced crossings.
evidence_signal: The model was validated against density-functional-theory band dispersions and shown to quantitatively capture spin splittings and leading Bloch-state spin-polarization patterns near the band edges.
watch_item: Because the Hamiltonian is an effective low-energy model with fitted parameters, it may not capture physics outside the band-edge regime or effects beyond the chosen symmetry-adapted hopping terms.
paper_title: Single-orbital tight-binding model for chiral one-dimensional hybrid organic-inorganic lead halide perovskites
